issues.description: Title/CHANGELOG/CheckID say 'single_network_interface' but PR description and semantics describe 'multiple_network_interfaces' — identity is complected with intent
issues.detail: The check name asserts a property (single interface) while the logic detects the violation (multiple interfaces) and the PR title says 'detect VMs with multiple network interfaces.' These are two different facts and the code is conflating them. A check is a *value* representing one assertion about the world; its name is its identity. Pick one framing and make name, title, status_extended, and PR all agree. Today a reader cannot tell from the CheckID alone whether PASS means 'has one' or 'has many' without reading the code.

issues.description: GKE-detection by name-prefix string-matching complects identity with classification — a fact ('is GKE-managed') is being inferred from a string
issues.detail: `instance.name.startswith("gke-")` is place-oriented thinking: the name is a place where we happen to read a classification out of. GKE-management is a fact about the instance (labels: `goog-gke-node`, or metadata, or managed instance group membership). Inferring it from a name prefix means any VM a user names `gke-foo` becomes MANUAL, and any real GKE node renamed becomes FAIL. Decompose: extract `is_gke_managed: bool` as a value on the Instance model in compute_service.py from the real signal (labels/metadata), and let the check read that value. The check then expresses one idea, not two.

issues.description: Metadata.json does not describe the MANUAL/GKE branch that the code implements — spec and implementation are out of sync
issues.detail: The metadata Description and Risk speak only of PASS/FAIL, but the code has a third outcome (MANUAL for GKE). The check's specification (the metadata, which is the public contract) and its implementation are complected: a user reading metadata cannot predict the behavior. Either drop the MANUAL branch (let GKE FAIL and document the exception) or update metadata to describe the three outcomes explicitly. Right now the docstring in the .py file is the only place the MANUAL semantics live.

issues.description: The 'no network interfaces' branch silently reports PASS with a misleading status — empty case is not thought through
issues.detail: When `interface_count == 0`, `report.status` was set to PASS at the top and is never changed; status_extended says 'has no network interfaces' but the finding reads as PASS. A VM with zero NICs is either impossible (GCE requires at least one) or a data-collection bug, not a passing security state. Decide: is this case essential (can it happen?) or incidental (a defensive branch that confuses readers)? If it cannot happen, remove the branch. If it can, it deserves its own status — not PASS.

issues.description: _get_instances now does two things in one loop: deriving public_ip and constructing NetworkInterface values — concerns are mildly complected
issues.detail: The loop in compute_service._get_instances walks `networkInterfaces` once for public_ip detection and then appends a NetworkInterface value in the same pass. That is acceptable but it means a single pass is doing two unrelated transformations. A cleaner decomposition: build the `network_interfaces` list as a pure transformation of the raw dicts, then derive `public_ip = any(nic has natIP)` from that list. The Instance model would then expose both facts from one source of truth, and public_ip and network_interfaces could not drift.

issues.description: NetworkInterface model drops accessConfigs / natIP / aliasIpRanges — the value is impoverished relative to the fact
issues.detail: The new NetworkInterface only carries name, network, subnetwork. The raw GCP fact includes accessConfigs (with natIP), networkIP, aliasIpRanges, stackType. Other checks (public_ip, ip_forwarding, alias-range exposure) already need or will need these. Either commit to NetworkInterface being a value that *fully* represents the interface (so other checks can be rewritten against it and the place-oriented `public_ip: bool` on Instance becomes derivable), or be explicit that it is intentionally partial. Right now we have introduced a second representation of the same fact without retiring the first.

issues.description: Tests assert exact English status_extended strings — TDD-as-design coupling that will break on copy edits
issues.detail: Six tests compare `status_extended` to exact sentences including punctuation. The thing under test is the *decision* (PASS/FAIL/MANUAL given N interfaces), not the wording. These assertions complect the behavior contract with the message string and will fire false negatives on harmless copy changes. Test the status, the resource identity, and the count/interface list; leave the prose to a single golden test if you need one at all.

issues.description: No test exercises a non-GKE instance whose name happens to start with 'gke-' — the name-prefix heuristic is untested at its boundary
issues.detail: The single behavioral subtlety in this check — name-prefix GKE detection — has exactly one test (a happy-path GKE node). There is no test for a user-named 'gke-bastion' VM, no test for a real GKE node renamed by an operator, no test for 'gke' without the trailing dash. If the heuristic is going to live, its boundary cases are the only thing worth testing about it. Better: replace the heuristic with a real signal (see other finding) and the test surface shrinks.

review.summary: The check is a simple fact-test (count NICs per instance) that has been quietly complected with three other concerns: a naming choice that asserts the opposite of what it detects, a GKE-classification inferred by string-prefix from the instance name, a MANUAL outcome that exists in code but not in metadata, and a partial NetworkInterface value that overlaps with the existing `public_ip` boolean without replacing it. The essential complexity here is one line: count network_interfaces, compare to 1. Everything else — GKE special-casing, the empty-list branch, the dual representation of NIC facts — is incidental, and most of it is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE: familiar Prowler patterns applied without asking whether the fact being read is the right fact. The hammock question that wasn't asked: what is a NetworkInterface, as a value, in this codebase, and should `public_ip`/`ip_forward` be derived from a list of them rather than carried alongside? Answer that and three of these findings collapse into one clean model change.
